plan.notes: Source: official University of Hartford suggested course sequence, 'Suggested Course Sequence - B. S. in Computer Science - AY 23-24' (PDF dated 1-May-23), hosted on the university's official site: https://WWW.HARTFORD.EDU/academics/schools-colleges/arts-sciences/_files/bs-cs-course-sequence-23-24.pdf . This AY 23-24 sequence is the latest official B.S. Computer Science term-by-term sequence found on hartford.edu (searched 2026-09-30; no AY 24-25 or 25-26 sequence exists). Degree name verified in the official catalog (catalog.hartford.edu, Computing Sciences): the department offers a B.A. and a B.S. in Computer Science ('Computer Science, B.S.'); this file is the B.S. The PDF was downloaded and transcribed with pdftotext -layout, then hand-mapped to the pipeline schema; course titles follow the sequence PDF, cross-checked against the catalog course list where shown (CS 114 Fundamentals of Computing I, CS 115 Fundamentals of Computing II, CS 211 Architecture and Assembly Language, CS 220P Data Structures, CS 460W Software Development). Credit total: the catalog (and the sequence's own notes) publish a minimum of 120 credit hours for graduation in the College of Arts and Sciences. The suggested sequence prints variable term totals (Junior Fall 13-16 due to the 0-3 credit LBC elective; Senior Spring 12-15 due to a 0-3 credit general elective). This file resolves those two slots to 3 credits (LBC) and 0 credits (optional general elective, flagged required_zero) so the summed total equals the published 120-credit minimum. Both resolutions sit inside the sequence's own printed ranges; students choosing different values land between 117 and 123 per the printed extremes. Prerequisites: the suggested-sequence PDF does not state course prerequisites, so all prereq fields are left empty rather than inferred; verify prereqs against the official catalog course descriptions. The 6 CS Elective slots equal the 18 CS-elective credits required by catalog note 7 (breadth-area rules documented in each slot's choice_note). Catalog honesty rules carried: minimum 2.25 overall average in the major; all major courses for letter grade (no Pass/No Pass). UIS = University Interdisciplinary Studies general-education courses; one Diversity-designated UIS course is required (catalog note 8).

courses.title: UIS: Artistic and Creative Expression
courses.choice_note: Student-choice UIS course designated Artistic and Creative Expression. Catalog note 8: one Diversity-designated course required from UIS electives.

courses.title: Humanities Elective
courses.choice_note: Student-choice humanities elective. Catalog note 1: humanities electives from 3 different disciplines: literature (ENG, not writing classes), foreign language (ARA, FR, GER, HBR, ITA, SPA), history (HIS), philosophy (PHI). Note 4: one Diversity and one Community/Citizenship course required across the humanities, social science, and arts electives.

courses.title: Social Science Elective
courses.choice_note: Student-choice social science elective. Catalog note 2: social science electives from 2 different disciplines: economics (EC), politics (POL), psychology (PSY), sociology (SOC). Note 4: one Diversity and one Community/Citizenship course required across the humanities, social science, and arts electives.

courses.title: UIS: Cultural and Historical Interpretation
courses.choice_note: Student-choice UIS course designated Cultural and Historical Interpretation. Catalog note 8: one Diversity-designated course required from UIS electives.

courses.title: CS Elective
courses.choice_note: Student-choice CS elective. Catalog note 7: 18 credits of CS electives required, including at least 12 credits of CS courses at the 300 level or above, with at least one course taken in each of the three breadth areas: (1) Systems: CS 353, CS 355, CS 451, CS 455, ECE 231/232; (2) Applications: CS 275, CS 280, CS 351, CS 365, CS 368, CS 371, CS 375, CS 380, HCID 220P, HCID 230, HCID 370; (3) Theory: CS 340, CS 342, M 220, M 222W. CS 330/331 and CS 290/291/390/391/490/491 are assigned to a breadth area by course content with department chair approval.
